messages:
claire: quick q — i collected a ~6GB nsys capture while investigating a kernel regression on dedicated (A10s). where should i drop this and what scrub steps do we need? cc @eng-runtime
micah: s3 is best for large bundles: s3://redwood-perf/traces/raw/ (private). add `owner=eng-runtime` tag. if it's PII-sensitive, use the secure bucket: s3://redwood-perf/traces/secure/ and ping infrajen for access.
yoichi: for KV-cache related traces include a short replay snippet that reproduces prefix hits (we need sequence IDs). also include `--nvtx` markers in the serving run so we can map op -> model stage.
claire: got it. what's our preferred filename pattern? i want something scriptable.
devex-ron: we standardized on a compact pattern (please use this): `env-model_hw-kvsize_runid_ts` example: `stg-llama-70b_a10s-kv64_r1234_1769804321` put `.nsys.tar.gz` at end. include a `meta.json` with keys: owner, experiment_id, model_commit, cmdline, input_snippet, redaction_level.
micah: small checklist: 1) run with nvtx/cuda capture 2) copy the raw `.qdrep` + `nvprof` logs 3) dump KV cache stats (`./serving --dump-kv-stats kvstats.json`) 4) include short synthetic prompt file (<=20 prompts).
claire: example command for us to recommend?
micah: yes — something like:
```bash
nsys profile --output trace-${USER}-${EXP} --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none \
  --launch-skip 0 --capture-range=env:PROFILE_START:PROFILE_END \
  ./bin/serve --model path/to/model --enable-kv-dump
```
then bundle:
```bash
tar -czf stg-llama-a10s-kv64_r1234_1769804321.nsys.tar.gz trace-*.qdrep kvstats.json meta.json input_prompts.json
```
yoichi: very important: redact customer identifiers from logs and prompts. common spots: `metadata.user_id`, `request.customer_id`, `input->attachments`. if you can't remove, replace with stable hash. we prefer `{redacted_user_x}` or sha256 truncated but note that even hashed PII may be sensitive — ask security if unsure.
claire: how strict are we on content redaction before uploading to the public raw bucket?
infrajen: public raw bucket = internal-only readable by Redwood employees, not external. still scrub anything that could identify a customer. for anything regulated, use the secure bucket and file an access request.
devex-ron: annotation tips for perfetto/nvtx timeline: add NVTX ranges around the following points: `request->tokenize`, `model->forward`, `kv->lookup`, `batch->merge`, `io->diskread`. keeps kernel timelines legible.
micah: for kernel selection analysis include a short CSV with per-kernel counts from `nsys stats` and our mapping table (kernel_name -> chosen_kernel_variant). we use that to correlate where the runtime selected a suboptimal kernel.
claire: any upstream scrub tool we should run automatically?
perf-bot: friendly reminder: there is a scrubber script in `infra/tools/scrub_trace.py` (run: `python infra/tools/scrub_trace.py --input bundle.tgz --level medium --output bundle.scrubbed.tgz`) — it strips common headers and replaces emails/uuids.
claire: perfect — i'll run that. one more: where do we log the analysis so the next person can find it?
devex-ron: put notes in the PR comment and attach the s3 path. also open a short thread in #eng-runtime with the link. for long-term storage, upload an annotated perfetto HTML to `s3://redwood-perf/traces/annotated/` with same basename and link it in the PR.
yoichi: when you upload, include a small `notes.md` explaining the suspect window (timestamps in qdrep), the KV hit rate, and any observed kernel fallbacks. even a few bullet points speed triage.
claire: thanks all — i'll scrub with the script, name it `stg-llama-a10s-kv64_r1234_1769804321.nsys.tar.gz`, upload to secure bucket, and post link here.
perf-bot: archived to s3://redwood-perf/traces/secure/stg-llama-a10s-kv64_r1234_1769804321.nsys.tar.gz (access requests required).
infrajen: noted, i'll grant micah and yoichi read access.
micah: once we have the bundle i'll run the quick kernel-diff script (`tools/kernel_diff.py --bundle <path>`) and post the top-5 candidates. :mag:
